----------
howdy, it’s Barsee again.

happy wednesday, AI family, and welcome back to AI Valley.

**here are the biggest things worth knowing today:**

* OpenAI releases findings on 377 math problems

* The state of the tech industry in 2026

* Plus trending AI tools, posts, and resources

Let’s _dive_ into the Valley of AI…


----------

----------
#### **WISPR FLOW**

## [Walk-and-think (capture ideas on the move)](https://ref.wisprflow.ai/aivalley)

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/da993fea-626b-46e5-ac5a-caccfc77851e/Newsletters_Image_1920x1080__7___8_.png?t=1791383325)
Caption: Courtesy: Wispr Flow

Some problems don't solve themselves at a keyboard. Flow is perfect for walks: talk through the idea, the structure, and the tradeoffs, then get back a clean draft you can paste into your doc or AI tool. It's like having a writing assistant that keeps up with your brain in motion.

[Try for free](https://ref.wisprflow.ai/aivalley)

~_*This is sponsored_~


----------

----------
#### **THROUGH THE VALLEY**

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/edf12a9c-9d62-49df-8020-be2eef446379/1791041393482__1_.png?t=1791384441)
Caption: Sam Altman. Photo: Heather Diehl/Getty Images

**OpenAI releases internal model’s findings on 377 math problems **- they give an internal model ~4000 open research problems and get [722 manuscripts](https://openai.com/index/sharing-ai-progress-in-mathematics/) proving 372 families of new results in number theory, theoretical computer science, physics, etc.

They claim to prove a "quasi-Riemann hypothesis", which while not the $1M Riemann Hypothesis from the Millennium Prize problems, is not far from it. For 162 of the manuscripts, they formalize the main result in Lean, which is then mechanically verified by a computer.

Most impressively, they claim to get almost all of these results in one prompt, taking on average ~3 hours of thinking compute on ChatGPT Pro. Their recent result on the Navier-Stokes equations used 10,000 AI agents.

Mathematician at Anthropic Levent Alpgge calls this "obviously the most significant moment in mathematical history":

They also talk about how devastating this is for young mathematicians who were hoping to make a career solving these problems. The same mathematician says that high school students are asking him "is there anything left for me to do in mathematics".

Soon AI will be spitting out new math faster than people can read it.


----------

----------
# TRENDING TOOLS


--------------------
* [diio](https://www.diio.com/us/starter-diio?utm_source=ai_valley&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=ai_valley_2026&utm_content=2026-10-07&utm_term=trending_ad_starte) > turns thousands of customer conversations into an intelligence layer AI can understand, reason over, and act on ~^(sponsored)^~

* [Core](https://x.com/zainmfj/status/2107146556176798081?s=20) - a personal AI computer that runs models entirely on device. It connects to your apps, files, and devices, builds context on your life over time, and works continuously to help you

* [Claude](https://x.com/claudeai/status/2107522596845822135?s=20) - now works inside Google Docs, Sheets, and Slides, and those files also open inside Claud

* [EmbeddingGemma 2](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/technology/developers-tools/embeddinggemma-2) - powers private search across text, photos, audio, and video that can run directly on a laptop, phone, or browser

* [iphone-use](https://github.com/leeguooooo/iphone-use) - gives an AI agent a real iPhone: the screen as text, tap, type and scroll over WebDriverAgent, with an honest answer for every action

* [Nano Banana 2.1](https://aistudio.google.com/prompts/new_chat?model=gemini-nano-banana-2.1&ref=producthunt) - Google's latest image generation and editing model

* [Incredible](https://x.com/useincredible/status/2107457256090411223?s=20) - personal AI assistant that learns by watching you do  your work

* [Manus 2.0](https://manus.im/blog/introducing-video-editor) - features a video editor that can edit, make shots, VO and more

* [Era](https://console.era.eon.io/) - a fake company to test enterprise agents

* [Beam](https://x.com/reflection_ai/status/2107186849370247235?s=20) - a highly efficient agentic open model with 501B total parameters and 23B active

* [Web Search API](https://developers.cloudflare.com/changelog/post/2026-10-02-introducing-web-search-api/?ref=producthunt) - lets your AI agents and applications search the Internet and ground their responses in live information

* [Hark Pro](https://x.com/adcock_brett/status/2107504425451536822?s=20) - now live on web, iOS, and Android

----------
# WHAT I'M CONSUMING


--------------------

newsletters.title: When Trying to Make AI Better Makes It Worse
newsletters.content:
A million words of failed drafts taught me that improving my AI setup sometimes means giving it fewer rules to follow  ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌
https://every.?ev_audience=free

Working Overtime

https://every.?ev_audience=free


WHEN TRYING TO MAKE AI BETTER MAKES IT WORSE https://every.?ev_audience=free


A MILLION WORDS OF FAILED DRAFTS TAUGHT ME THAT IMPROVING MY AI SETUP SOMETIMES MEANS GIVING IT FEWER RULES TO FOLLOW https://every.?ev_audience=free

by Katie Parrott https://every.?ev_audience=free

Midjourney/Every illustration.

Was this newsletter forwarded to you? Sign up https://every.?ev_audience=free to get it in your inbox.



----------------------------------------

It is a well-known fact that the Germans have a word for everything. Kummerspeck, literally “grief bacon,” is the weight you put on from emotional eating. Torschlusspanik, “gate-closing panic,” is the fear that time is running out to do the thing you’re supposed to do with your life.



Recently, I came across another gem: Verschlimmbesserung, or “worsen-bettering.” It refers to our desire to make something better, only to make it worse. Used in a sentence: “Ich habe meinen Kontext verschlimmbessert,” or “I have worsen-bettered my context.”

That’s precisely what I did to the context that drives my AI setup over a few weeks in September. By “context,” I’m referring to the style guides, examples, and instructions that tell Claude and ChatGPT who I am, how I write, and what I’m working on. When my context is good, my AI “assistants” can find what they need to do work the way I want them to do it—including writing essay drafts https://every.?ev_audience=free the way I want them written.

But a few weeks ago, my context went bad, and so did my work. Drafts came back crowded and flat. When I told the model what was wrong, the next draft came back worse. The system I’d built to keep me afloat started pulling me down with it. For a while, I stopped trusting my context. Then I stopped trusting myself.

You don’t need an elaborate setup to run into this problem. You might have asked your AI to keep answers short, then found yourself fighting it for a thorough explanation, or saved a successful draft as an example and watched its quirks turn up in everything that followed. A preference that helps with one task can get in the way of the next, especially when it has to coexist with everything else you’ve ever asked the model to remember.

**1/ Reflection is about to drop a big American open-weight AI model** - the Nvidia-backed startup is [reportedly](https://www.axios.com/2026/10/04/reflection-open-weight-ai) preparing to release its first model, aimed squarely at Chinese open models like Kimi and Qwen. It probably won't beat the absolute best models from OpenAI, Anthropic or Google at launch, but Axios says it'll be competitive with the top Chinese open-weight models.

That's actually important because China pretty much dominates the high-end open-weight model market right now. Reflection is trying to build a Western alternative that companies can download, customize and run themselves instead of sending everything through OpenAI or Anthropic's APIs.

But the bigger plan is something Reflection calls an “AI factory.” Basically, give it your company's private data, Reflection's models and a bunch of Nvidia GPUs, and you can build your own proprietary AI system. For companies sitting on really valuable data, like banks, hedge funds or even governments, that's a pretty compelling pitch.

The model is apparently coming soon, alongside several other Western open-weight models this month.

**2/ Trump just created a “Super Intelligence Force”** - [yes](https://truthsocial.com/@realDonaldTrump/posts/117382616783706638), that's actually what it's called. After telling the US government to start calling AI “Super Intelligence” last week, Trump has now named Director of National Intelligence [Jay Clayton](https://www.politico.com/news/2026/10/04/jay-clayton-ai-trump-01106137) as his AI czar and put him in charge of a new White House task force focused on it.

The group has 120 days to study the risks and opportunities of AI and recommend what Washington should actually do about it, including how to handle AI incidents, cyberattacks and advanced models going wrong.

Clayton seems pretty firmly on the acceleration side. He says the risk of America _not_ being first in AI is high and has pushed back on calls to pause development. Basically, figure out how to make this stuff safer without slowing the US down.

And apparently we're really committing to the whole “SI” thing now. [Elon Musk says](https://www.reuters.com/business/media-telecom/musk-says-he-will-rename-spacexai-spacexsi-2026-10-04/) he's renaming SpaceXAI to SpaceXSI.

**3/ OpenAI is putting ads inside image generation** - OpenAI is [testing a new ad format](https://openai.com/index/new-chatgpt-ads-format-and-measurement/) that shows sponsored products and experiences while you're generating images in ChatGPT, starting in the US later this month.

The ads will be labeled and kept separate from your actual content, and OpenAI says advertising still won't influence ChatGPT's answers. But image generation is a pretty interesting place to put them. Ask ChatGPT to design your living room, generate an outfit or visualize a new desk setup, and there are suddenly a lot of products that could naturally be advertised alongside what you're making.

No pricing yet, and OpenAI hasn't announced a way to opt out of these image-generation ads.
